name: South Face Left
descent_text: The route tops out on the West Ridge a short way below the summit. Either reverse the West Ridge, Class 3-4 with a few low fifth-class moves, rappelling or downclimbing most of it to the notch near 5,800 ft at its foot and dropping back into Commonwealth Basin; or descend the Southeast Ridge to Red Pass (about 5,400 ft), Class 3-4 with one rappel of about 80 ft, then follow the Commonwealth Basin trail about 4.5 miles back to the trailhead.
approach: Follow the Commonwealth Creek trail (PCT to Commonwealth Creek trail) until soon after crossing a stream and moving onto the flank of Red Mountain; leave the trail and follow the side valley below Lundin up to the base of its south face.
overview: A harder, more sustained line up the center of Lundin's south face, starting up an obvious hand-crack layback and finishing near the top of the West Ridge.
beta: Start at an obvious hand-crack layback feature near the center and lowest point of the south face. The crux pitch is 5.10 (sometimes wet). Climb upward and slightly left to gain a left-trending ramp, then exit rightward in the upper section via easier 5.7-5.8 climbing to meet the West Ridge near the summit.
